mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate increases borrowing and spending, stimulating economic growth and leading to higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when the federal funds rate is below 0.5, or the effect of the federal funds rate on stock prices is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative during periods of payroll employment growth, or the correlation between payroll employment and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when industrial production is above 95, or the effect of industrial production on stock prices is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts indicates decreased economic activity, leading to lower demand for goods and services, which in turn drives down stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when housing starts are below 600, or the effect of housing starts on stock prices is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate and a decrease in GDP indicate a tightening monetary cycle and decreased economic activity, leading to lower stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when the federal funds rate is above 1 and GDP is below 13000, or the joint effect of the federal funds rate and GDP on stock prices is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate and a decrease in payroll employment indicate a weak labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and lower stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when the unemployment rate is above 8 and payroll employment is below 130000, or the joint effect of the unemployment rate and payroll employment on stock prices is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales and a decrease in housing starts indicate increased consumer spending and decreased economic activity, leading to higher stock prices in the short term but lower stock prices in the long term, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days but negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when retail sales are above 400000 and housing starts are below 600, or the joint effect of retail sales and housing starts on stock prices is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
